docs.title: preprocessing(cfg, out_dir)
docs.text:
First stage of the 3-stage envelope pipeline: per-voxel obstruction scoring.

Converts a maximum-volume mesh and a set of insolation test surfaces into a 3-D scalar field where each voxel carries a score indicating how much it blocks sun or sky from the test surfaces. The steps are:

  1. Voxelization: the maximum-volume mesh is rasterized into a cubic occupancy grid with edge length cfg.voxel_size. This and the next two steps run in a local frame whose origin is the max volume's minimum corner; persisted coordinates are shifted back to world space.
  2. Surface sampling: the test surfaces are point-sampled (spacing cfg.grid_step), giving test points with outward normals. The test surface PLY file may contain several disjoint mesh components (e.g. separate facade panels, a ground plane and a courtyard, or a PV array). All components are sampled and their ray contributions added into a single score grid.

  3. Ray casting: for every test point, rays are cast through the voxel grid according to the configured mode. Each voxel that blocks a ray accumulates a weight that depends on the mode:

  4. time-based: sun-position rays for the configured analysis period; a voxel's score is the protected-surface area it shades times the duration, in m²·h (each sample point stands for ~grid_step² m²).

  5. tilted_plane: one ray per sample point at the plane angle; a non-zero score means the voxel lies on or above at least one plane.
  6. sky-patch modes (irradiance, benefit, daylight, radiative_cooling): rays go toward the sky patches, each patch carrying a mode-specific weight; a voxel's score is the sum of the weights of the rays it blocks times the area each sample point stands for (grid_step²): the solar energy it blocks in kWh (irradiance, benefit), or the sky it hides in m² of fully hidden sky (daylight, radiative_cooling; their weights sum to 1).

Persisted artifacts

An empty list when the projection failed; massing then uses the voxel footprint. test_points.npy, test_normals.npy, analysis_mesh.json Sample points (world coordinates), their normals, and the analysis mesh, for diagnostics and Grasshopper display. patch_weights.npy Per-sky-patch weights (sky-patch modes only). manifest.json Machine-readable manifest (PreprocessingManifest) recording a random run_id (new on every run), grid shape, world origin, voxel size, mode, score kind and score unit, and file paths relative to the manifest's folder. Written last, so a failed run leaves no manifest. diagnostics/ diagnostic.json (summary statistics and wall/CPU timings), config_snapshot.json, and, with cfg.diagnostic_plots, the score histogram and sky-patch weight plots.

Writes mask.npy and scores_compared_with_cutoff.npy (float32, the grid shape: the values the cutoff is applied to before the slope limit, which are the carve_above removal cutoffs when carve_above is on and the smoothed scores otherwise); the diagnostics record max_slope_deg, slope_limit_extra_voxels_removed and obstruction_fraction_carved_by_slope_limit.

thresholding(volume: Union[str, Path], cfg: Union[user_config, str, Path], out_dir: Union[str, Path]) -> ThresholdingResult

Second stage of the 3-stage pipeline: score-to-mask binarisation.

Loads the per-voxel obstruction scores produced by :func:preprocessing and applies a threshold strategy to produce a Boolean mask indicating which voxels to retain in the final envelope (True = keep, False = carve away).

For violation_count scores (time-based / tilted_plane modes), only a numeric threshold (cutoff) is accepted and applied directly.

Threshold strategies (set via cfg.threshold; the config layer normalizes every accepted spelling into a ThresholdSpec, and cfg.resolved_threshold() fills in the mode default when it is unset):

  • cutoff (shorthand: a bare number): a literal cutoff; voxels with score <= value are kept.
  • headtail: head/tail breaks (Jiang 2013). The scores are split at their mean; while the part above the mean (the head) holds at most 40 % of the values, the head is split again at its own mean. The last such mean is the cutoff. Suited to the heavy-tailed score distributions common in urban solar access studies.
  • carve_fraction (default for weighted modes): cumulative-score cutoff. It finds the cutoff at which the removed voxels hold the given fraction of the building's total score mass, counting the voxels that carve_above removes along with them.

All threshold statistics, retention counts and smoothing use occupied voxels only; the mask is False on empty cells. With carve_above (the default), occupied voxels above a carved run in their column are removed as well. Then, for the score-cutoff methods of the weighted modes (or whenever max_slope_deg is set), columns that rise more steeply than max_slope_deg above their surroundings are cut down (:func:~urbansolarcarver.column_postprocessing.limit_column_slope); this removes some score beyond the fraction, reported as obstruction_fraction_carved_by_slope_limit. mask.npy is the final mask that gets exported.

Score smoothing (cfg.score_smoothing):

Before thresholding, a Gaussian blur can be applied to the continuous score volume to smooth resolution-dependent noise. This produces a cleaner binary mask (and carved mesh) at fine voxel sizes.

  • None (default): auto, 1.1 × voxel_size metres.
  • 0: disabled, no smoothing.
  • Positive float: explicit radius (Gaussian sigma) in metres. Rule of thumb: keep close to voxel_size (1.0–1.2×). Values above 2× voxel_size over-smooth and round features.

Only applied to weighted-score modes (irradiance, benefit, daylight, radiative_cooling). Violation-count modes (time-based, tilted_plane) are unaffected.

To tune carve_fraction against a performance target, compare obstruction_fraction_carved in diagnostics/diagnostic.json across runs.

Third stage of the 3-stage pipeline: mesh extraction from the binary mask.

Loads the Boolean voxel mask produced by :func:thresholding and the occupancy grid persisted during :func:preprocessing, combines them (logical AND), and converts the resulting carved voxel field into a triangle mesh suitable for downstream CAD / BIM / visualisation workflows.

Mesh extraction proceeds through :func:~urbansolarcarver.meshing.finalize_mesh, which supports two strategies (selected by cfg.apply_smoothing):

  • cubic (apply_smoothing=False, default): a 3x3x3 neighbour filter first drops isolated voxels, then the exposed faces of the occupied voxels are emitted; fast, produces the classic voxel look.
  • smoothed (apply_smoothing=True): the binary field is converted to a signed-distance field, smoothed, and iso-surfaced with Marching Cubes, then polished with cfg.smooth_iters Taubin passes (0-6).

On both paths, connected voxel clusters smaller than cfg.min_voxels and mesh fragments with fewer than cfg.min_face_count faces are removed. The mesh uses the voxel size and origin recorded by preprocessing; the config's voxel_size is not read.

docs.text:
Fourth stage: floor plates that follow the footprint, from the carved envelope.

Floors are ground_floor_height then floor_height tall, counted from the lowest point of the maximum volume. The footprint (the plan projection of the maximum volume that preprocessing saved as footprint.json, not the mesh named in cfg) is split into faces, one per facade, and each face into square modules of min_plate_dimension, cut along its facade and in depth behind it. A module is built on a floor when it stays in the maximum volume over the floor's full height, at most plate_tolerance of its volume lies outside the carved envelope, and (with plate_stacking: supported) it is built on the floor below. See :mod:urbansolarcarver.floor_plates.

docs.title: Ray Tracing
docs.text:
Ray generation and voxel traversal for the carving pipeline, in two modules. The main kernels use a DDA (Digital Differential Analyzer) that steps each ray through the voxel grid and adds to a per-voxel volume in a single pass.

ray_tracing.py builds and traces the rays:

  • trace_and_score_dda: traces a batch of rays and adds each ray's weight to every voxel it crosses (weighted modes). Runs on CUDA or on Warp's CPU backend.
  • trace_and_count_dda: the same traversal, adding a count of 1 per ray (time-based and tilted_plane).
  • follow_mass_behind_skin_dda: the skin rule, which keeps a test surface's skin voxels with the mass behind them.
  • generate_sky_patch_rays / generate_sun_rays: expand sample points × directions into flat ray arrays (origins + directions), keeping only directions the surface faces.
  • auto_batch_size: picks a ray batch size from the free GPU memory, to avoid out-of-memory errors on large scenes.

warp_kernels.py sets up Warp and holds every Warp kernel of the package (the DDA kernels above and the parity voxelizer that voxelization.voxelize_solid_warp launches), so Warp compiles and caches them as one module:

  • dda_backend_available: whether the Warp DDA backend can run on a device.
  • require_dda_backend: raises WarpBackendUnavailableError, naming the reason, when it cannot. Ray tracing has no other backend; every carver calls this first.
  • warmup_kernels: precompiles the Warp kernels (urbansolarcarver warmup).

Rays are processed in batches. With ray_batch_size: 0 (the default) the batch size comes from auto_batch_size; set a positive value to fix it.

docs.title: UrbanSolarCarver: ray generation and voxel grid traversal
docs.text:
This module builds rays (sample point to sky patch, or sample point to sun, keeping only directions the surface faces) and traces them through the voxel grid for the carving pipeline.

Rays are traced with the DDA (digital differential analyzer, Amanatides & Woo 1987) Warp kernels of :mod:warp_kernels, launched here, on CUDA or on Warp's CPU backend. The fused wrappers (:func:trace_and_score_dda, :func:trace_and_count_dda) add each ray's weight or a count of 1 directly into a per-voxel volume, so no list of hits is stored. There is no other tracer: when Warp cannot run, the carvers raise WarpBackendUnavailableError (see :func:warp_kernels.require_dda_backend).

The coordinate conventions are those of :mod:warp_kernels.

docs.title: follow_mass_behind_skin_dda(min_corner, scale, resolution, origins, ray_dirs, point_ids, surface_normals, occupancy, values, ray_length)
docs.text:
Return values with every own-skin voxel raised to the value of the voxel behind it.

A voxel the source surface's plane passes through is that surface's skin. When the skin voxel and the voxel behind it are both occupied, the skin belongs to the mass behind the surface: its own rays do not count it, but it must not outlast that mass. So each skin voxel a ray visits takes the maximum of its value and the value of the voxel behind it (counts: removed when the mass behind is removed; scores: never below the mass behind).

The voxel behind a skin voxel is found by stepping from the skin voxel's centre one cell length at a time against the surface normal, up to three steps, until the voxel containing the stepped point lies wholly behind the plane.

docs.title: UrbanSolarCarver: Warp setup and kernels
docs.text:
Initializes NVIDIA Warp, tells whether its exact DDA backend can run on a device (:func:dda_backend_available), precompiles the kernels (:func:warmup_kernels), and defines every Warp kernel of the package:

  • the DDA traversal (digital differential analyzer, Amanatides & Woo 1987): one thread per ray, stepping from voxel to voxel and visiting every voxel the ray crosses exactly once, with fused kernels that add each ray's weight or a count of 1 directly into a per-voxel volume, and the kernel of the skin rule;
  • the parity voxelizer used by :func:voxelization.voxelize_solid_warp.

All kernels live in this one module on purpose: Warp compiles a Python module as one unit and caches it on disk by module, so :func:warmup_kernels compiles them all at once. The kernels exist only when Warp imports and initializes (_warp_available). Their launch wrappers are in :mod:ray_tracing and :mod:voxelization.

References

Amanatides, J. & Woo, A. (1987). "A Fast Voxel Traversal Algorithm for Ray Tracing." Eurographics '87, pp. 3-10.

Coordinate conventions
  • World to grid: grid_idx = floor((world_pt - origin) / cell_size)
  • Cell size: cell_size = scale / resolution (meters per voxel)
  • Flat index: x * resolution**2 + y * resolution + z (row-major, C order)
  • floor maps a point to the voxel that contains it; rounding would shift every index by half a voxel.

docs.title: warmup_kernels(device=None)
docs.text:
Compile (or load from the on-disk cache) this module's Warp kernels for device now instead of on first use.

Warp compiles all kernels in a module on the first launch. This costs roughly 3-10 s once per machine, device and code version; afterwards the compiled binaries load from Warp's disk cache in milliseconds. Calling this during installation (setup_env.py), at daemon startup, or via usc warmup moves that cost to a moment where the user already expects to wait, so the first carving run is not slowed by it.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default device device | str | None

Target device. None resolves like cfg.device='auto': CUDA when available, else the Warp CPU backend.

None

Returns:

Type Description bool

True if the kernels are ready on the device (compiled or cached); False if Warp is unavailable or compilation failed. When only the precompilation failed, the kernels compile on first use instead.

docs.title: Scoring
docs.text:
Sky-patch weight dispatch and threshold selection:

  • Weight dispatch (get_weights): calls the sky-patch weighting function for the selected mode (Perez irradiance, heating benefit, CIE daylight luminance, or radiative cooling).
  • Thresholds, applied by the thresholding stage to the raw scores of the occupied voxels:
    • carve_fraction_threshold: the cutoff above which the voxels hold a given fraction of the total score mass.
    • headtail_threshold: Jiang (2013) head/tail breaks for heavy-tailed score distributions.
    • A numeric cutoff from the config is used as given.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.scoring
docs.text:
UrbanSolarCarver scoring module

Sky-patch weight computation and threshold selection for voxel carving.

  1. get_weights(mode, device, epw_file, hoys, …) → torch.Tensor Per-patch weight vector for the specified mode. Delegates to compute_EPW_based_weights (sky_patches.py) for irradiance, benefit and daylight, and to compute_radiative_cooling_weights for radiative_cooling. Inside a CarverSession the result is cached, keyed by every argument and by the contents of the EPW and simulated-weights files, so a preprocessing run with unchanged weather settings skips the sky matrix.

  2. carve_fraction_threshold(scores, fraction) → float Score cutoff above which the highest-scoring voxels hold fraction of the total score.

  3. headtail_threshold(scores) → float Head/tail breaks (Jiang 2013): repeatedly splits a right-skewed score distribution at its arithmetic mean. Suited to obstruction scores, which are usually heavy-tailed.

docs.title: get_weights(mode, device=None, epw_file=None, hoys=None, dew_point_celsius=14.0, bliss_k=1.8, balance_temperature=15.0, balance_offset=2.0, north_deg=0.0, min_sky_elevation_deg=0.0, include_harm=False, simulated_weights_path=None)
docs.text:
Return one weight per Tregenza sky patch for the given analysis mode.

  • irradiance: cumulative direct + diffuse irradiance per patch over the hours in hoys (kWh/m²), from the EPW via a Ladybug sky matrix.
  • benefit: the same, counted only in hours below the heating balance point (balance_temperature minus balance_offset); with include_harm, irradiance in hours above balance_temperature plus balance_offset is subtracted (clipped at 0).
  • daylight: CIE standard overcast sky luminance; needs no EPW.
  • radiative_cooling: long-wave cooling potential from the dew point (Martin-Berdahl emissivity, Bliss angular law), normalized to sum to 1.

'time-based' and 'tilted_plane' do not use sky-patch weights and raise ValueError here.

Inside a CarverSession the weights are cached (see the module notes): the returned tensor may be shared, so callers must not modify it.

docs.title: carve_fraction_threshold(scores, fraction, mass=None)
docs.text:
Score-mass cutoff: the threshold above which voxels collectively account for fraction of the total score mass.

Equivalent to sorting all scores descending and walking the cumulative sum until it reaches fraction * total. With mass, the voxels are ranked by scores but the sum counts mass (thresholding ranks by the cutoff at which carve_above removes a voxel and counts each voxel's own score, so the fraction includes what carve_above removes). A full sort of a large grid is O(N log N) and takes seconds to minutes at 300³ voxels and above, so this implementation makes two O(N) passes instead:

  1. A weighted histogram locates the bin containing the cutoff.
  2. Only the scores inside that single bin (N / n_bins expected) are sorted exactly, reproducing the argsort result.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default scores ndarray

Array of non-negative voxel scores (any shape).

required fraction float

Fraction of the total score mass to carve, in [0, 1].

required mass ndarray

Non-negative mass of each voxel, same shape as scores; default scores itself.

None

Returns:

Type Description float

Threshold value; voxels scoring strictly above it are carved.

docs.title: headtail_threshold(scores, max_iterations=50, head_limit=0.4)
docs.text:
Head/tail breaks cutoff (Jiang, 2013).

Split the scores at their mean. If the part above the mean (the head) is a minority (at most head_limit of the values), the mean is a valid break; split the head again at its own mean, and so on. Stop when the head is no longer a minority (or is empty).

Returns the last valid break, so only the heaviest obstructors score above it. If even the first split has a majority head (no heavy tail), the overall mean is returned.

Example: 80 values of 1, 16 of 10 and 4 of 100 give breaks 6.4 (head 20 %) and 28 (head 20 %), then an empty head: the cutoff is 28.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
Compute-session management. A CarverSession keeps the CUDA context alive across pipeline calls and holds a value cache for results that are expensive to rebuild (voxelized grids, Tregenza patch directions and solid angles, and the sky-patch weights of the weighted modes). Compiled Warp kernels are cached by Warp itself, on disk.

Cache keys cover everything a value depends on (for a voxel grid: a hash of the mesh, voxel size, margin and device), so an entry stays valid for later runs. The cache holds at most max_cache_bytes (1 GiB by default) and drops the least recently used entries beyond that. The Grasshopper daemon runs one long-lived session and keeps its cache between commands, so re-running preprocessing on unchanged geometry skips voxelization; after each command it returns only unused GPU memory to the driver. The Python API and CLI run without a session unless you open one with with CarverSession():. The session_cache decorator stores a function's result in the active session under a key built from its arguments.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.session
docs.text:
Long-lived compute session shared by consecutive pipeline runs.

CarverSession keeps the CUDA context alive (the daemon holds one for its whole lifetime) and caches values that are expensive to rebuild, such as voxel grids and the Tregenza patch directions and solid angles. Compiled Warp kernels are cached by Warp itself, on disk.

Cache keys must describe everything the cached value depends on, including the device it lives on, so an entry can be reused by any later run. The cache holds at most max_cache_bytes of arrays and tensors and drops the least recently used entries beyond that; bump() clears it.

Public API: CarverSession context manager owning the cache get_active_session the session registered for a device, if any session_cache decorator caching a function's result in the session

The wrapped function accepts an extra session= keyword; otherwise the active session is used. Without a session the function simply runs, and if the key cannot be formatted from the call's arguments it runs uncached, with a one-time log warning.

docs.title: Simulated Weights
docs.text: Simulated benefit weights: an ISO 13790 Annex C hourly thermal model ("5R1C") plus perturbation attribution, producing the hourly benefit / harm series consumed by benefit mode's simulated_weights_path. See Carving Modes for the user-level workflow and Tutorial 5 for a walkthrough.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.simulated_weights
docs.text:
Simulated benefit weights for benefit mode (ISO 13790 5R1C).

Implements the ISO 13790 Annex C simple hourly method ("5R1C": five thermal conductances and one heat capacity, as an electrical-circuit analogue of a single building zone) and derives, by perturbation, the marginal benefit and harm of solar gain at every hour of the year:

benefit[t] = -dQ_heating / dPhi_sol(t)   in [0, 1]
harm[t]    = +dQ_cooling / dPhi_sol(t)   in [0, 1]

Q_heating and Q_cooling are the annual demands [Wh] and Phi_sol(t) is the solar gain entering the zone in hour t [W]. The two series are written to a simulated_weights.json artifact that benefit mode can use in place of its balance-point Heaviside filter.

Provenance: this is an independent implementation written directly from the ISO 13790 Annex C equation set (not a fork or port of an existing simulator). It is cross-validated against ETH Zurich's RC_BuildingSimulator (MIT, https://github.com/architecture-building-systems/RC_BuildingSimulator; Jayathissa et al., Applied Energy 202, 2017) on three archetype scenarios (medium office, heavy masonry, light insulated) driven by the bundled Golden TMY3 EPW. The reference simulator's derived conductances are fed in directly, so the comparison tests the hourly recurrence: annual heating and cooling demands agree within 1 Wh (or a relative 1e-6), and hourly air and mass temperatures and demands agree at sampled hours. Reference data: tests/data/oracle_5r1c_reference.json; regression: tests/test_simulated_weights.py. Design, coefficient provenance, and declared limitations: design/simulated-weights.md; user-level documentation: docs/simulated-weights.md.

This module is deliberately NumPy-only at import time (no torch, no ladybug) so it stays usable as a standalone generator; the EPW-facing helper imports Ladybug lazily.

docs.title: ZoneParams(floor_area, h_tr_em, h_tr_w, h_tr_is, h_tr_ms, h_ve, c_m, a_m, a_t, t_set_heating=ARCHETYPE_DEFAULTS['t_set_heating'], t_set_cooling=ARCHETYPE_DEFAULTS['t_set_cooling']) dataclass
docs.text:
5R1C parameters: conductances (h_*) in W/K, c_m in J/K, areas (floor_area, a_m, a_t) in m², set-points in °C.

h_tr_em is exterior to mass, h_tr_w windows, h_tr_is air to internal surfaces, h_tr_ms surfaces to mass, h_ve ventilation.

Use :meth:from_archetype to derive them from physical archetype inputs per the standard; tests may also construct directly from known conductances (e.g. values from the reference simulator).

docs.title: from_archetype(floor_area, volume, u_opaque, area_opaque, u_window, area_window, ach_vent, ach_infiltration, heat_recovery=ARCHETYPE_DEFAULTS['heat_recovery'], mass_class=ARCHETYPE_DEFAULTS['mass_class'], t_set_heating=ARCHETYPE_DEFAULTS['t_set_heating'], t_set_cooling=ARCHETYPE_DEFAULTS['t_set_cooling']) classmethod
docs.text:
Derive the network from archetype inputs per ISO 13790.

  • A_tot = 4.5 · A_f; H_tr,is = 3.45 · A_tot
  • (A_m, C_m) from the Table-12 mass class
  • H_tr,ms = 9.1 · A_m
  • H_tr,op = U_opaque · A_opaque; H_tr,w = U_window · A_window
  • H_tr,em = 1 / (1/H_tr,op − 1/H_tr,ms) (§12.2.2 serial split)
  • H_ve = 1200 · b_ek · V · ACH_tot/3600, with 1200 J/(m³K) the volumetric heat capacity of air and the heat-recovery adjustment b_ek = 1 − (ACH_vent/ACH_tot) · η_hr (Annex E).

Units: areas in m², volume in m³, U-values in W/(m²K), air change rates in 1/h, heat_recovery (η_hr) as a fraction 0-1, set-points in °C.

Raises ValueError for an unknown mass_class, when H_tr,op >= H_tr,ms (the serial split would be negative or infinite), or when the total air change rate is not positive.

docs.title: simulate(p, t_out, phi_int, phi_sol, t_m_init=20.0)
docs.text:
Annual 5R1C simulation of a single zone (Wh demands, °C series).

t_out, phi_int and phi_sol are hourly arrays of length 8760: outdoor dry-bulb [°C], internal gains [W], transmitted solar gains [W]. t_m_init is the mass temperature at the start of the year [°C]. Raises ValueError if an array does not have shape (8760,).

docs.title: attribute_solar_gains(p, t_out, phi_int, phi_sol, eps=1.0, t_m_init=20.0)
docs.text:
Marginal hourly benefit/harm of solar gain by central-difference perturbation.

Returns (benefit, harm), each (8760,) in [0, 1]: the fraction of one extra watt-hour of solar gain at hour t that offsets heating demand / becomes cooling load over the year. eps is the perturbation size [W]; the other arguments are as in :func:simulate.

Values are marginal at this archetype's operating point. At hours where the control switches between heating, free-floating and cooling, the derivative is not defined and the central difference gives an average of the one-sided slopes. Out-of-range values up to 0.02 from such switching are clipped silently; larger ones are also clipped but trigger a warning.

docs.title: transmitted_solar_from_epw(epw_path, windows, hourly_factors=None)
docs.text:
Hourly transmitted solar gain [W] for a set of vertical windows.

windows: sequence of (azimuth_deg, area_m2, g_value); azimuth in Ladybug convention (0 = N, 90 = E, 180 = S, 270 = W); g_value is the glazing's total solar energy transmittance (0-1). The irradiance on each window plane [W/m²] comes from Ladybug's Wea.directional_irradiance for a vertical surface (isotropic sky, ground reflectance 0.2, no obstructions); it is multiplied by area and g_value.

hourly_factors: optional per-window hourly transmission multipliers (one (8760,) array per window, e.g. shading coefficients); default 1.

Returns an (8760,) array of the summed gain over all windows [W].

docs.text:
Write the simulated_weights.json artifact and return its path.

The schema is described in design/simulated-weights.md. Values are rounded to 6 decimals. Raises ValueError if either series is not 8760 finite values in [0, 1].

docs.title: read_simulated_weights(path)
docs.text:
Read and validate a simulated_weights.json artifact.

Returns (benefit, harm, meta): two (8760,) float64 arrays and the metadata dict. Raises ValueError if the file cannot be read or parsed, has an unsupported schema_version, or holds invalid series.

docs.title: expand_shoebox(archetype)
docs.text:
Expand the shoebox geometry shorthand into explicit archetype areas.

Instead of floor_area / volume / area_opaque / area_window / windows, an archetype may describe a rectangular single-zone box:

  • width: east-west dimension (m)
  • length: north-south dimension (m)
  • height: storey height (m)
  • wwr: window-to-wall ratio per facade in [0, 1), keyed by cardinal name (north / east / south / west); omitted sides get no window
  • g_value: glazing solar transmittance for all windows (default 0.6)
  • orientation: degrees to rotate the box clockwise from north (optional, default 0)

Derived: floor area = width x length; volume = floor area x height; per-facade window areas = wwr x facade area; area_opaque = opaque walls + roof (ground slab excluded); area_window = sum of windows. Archetypes without any of the shoebox keys above are returned as an unchanged copy.

Raises ValueError if the shoebox keys are incomplete, mixed with explicit-area keys, non-positive, or define no window.

docs.title: generate_simulated_weights(epw_path, archetype, out_path, internal_gains_w_m2=None, eps=1.0)
docs.text:
Run the full 5R1C weights pipeline: EPW + archetype → artifact.

archetype holds the :meth:ZoneParams.from_archetype keyword arguments plus windows: a list of [azimuth_deg, area_m2, g_value] (or the shoebox geometry shorthand, see :func:expand_shoebox). Optional keys: shading_permanent, shading_hot and hot_months (transmission multipliers, see :func:_shading_factors), and the internal-gain keys below.

Internal gains are either a single flat value [W/m²] or a 24-value daily occupancy profile [W/m² per hour of day], tiled over the year. They may come from the internal_gains_w_m2 / internal_gains_profile_w_m2 archetype keys, or be passed as the internal_gains_w_m2 argument (which takes precedence). Default 5.0.

eps is the solar-gain perturbation [W] used by :func:attribute_solar_gains. Writes the JSON artifact to out_path and, if matplotlib is installed, a heatmap PNG next to it with the same name; returns the artifact path.

docs.title: Sky Patches
docs.text:
Implements the Tregenza hemisphere subdivision (145 patches) used by all weighted carving modes. Each patch represents a solid-angle region of the sky dome; the weighting functions assign a weight to each patch depending on the analysis mode.

  • Tregenza geometry: 145 direction vectors and their solid angles, following the standard subdivision used in climate-based daylight modelling.
  • EPW-based weights (compute_EPW_based_weights): for irradiance and benefit, builds a cumulative sky matrix of direct and diffuse irradiance from an EPW weather file with the Perez all-weather sky model. Benefit keeps only hours with outdoor temperature below the balance point, or scales each hour by simulated weights. For daylight, returns the CIE overcast luminance distribution without reading an EPW.
  • Radiative cooling weights (compute_radiative_cooling_weights): long-wave cooling potential per patch from the Martin-Berdahl clear-sky emissivity with Bliss angular attenuation.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.sky_patches
docs.text:
UrbanSolarCarver Sky Patch Weighting Module

Generates sky-patch direction vectors, solid angles, and per-patch weight distributions for the voxel carving pipeline. P = 145 Tregenza patches.

Core Functions

  1. fetch_tregenza_patch_directions(device) → torch.Tensor Lazily loads a Ladybug ViewSphere and returns a (P×3) tensor of unit vectors for the P Tregenza sky patches.

  2. fetch_tregenza_patch_solid_angles(device) → torch.Tensor Returns a length-P tensor of solid angles (steradians) per patch.

  3. compute_EPW_based_weights(mode, epw_path, hoys, device, ...) → torch.Tensor Per-patch weights for the modes time-based (uniform), daylight (CIE overcast sky), irradiance and benefit (climate-based, from a Ladybug SkyMatrix built with the Perez all-weather model; units kWh/m²).

  4. compute_radiative_cooling_weights(dewpoint_celsius, bliss_k, device, min_elevation_deg) → torch.Tensor Theoretical long-wave radiative cooling potential per patch (Martin-Berdahl sky emissivity with Bliss angular variation). Assumes a horizontal analysis surface.

The weights are combined with per-voxel sky-patch visibility to accumulate exposure scores. The Tregenza vectors and solid angles are also usable on their own for diagnostics or custom weighting schemes.

docs.title: fetch_tregenza_patch_directions(device)
docs.text:
Return the 145 unit direction vectors of the Tregenza hemisphere subdivision (Tregenza, 1987). The dome divides the sky hemisphere into 145 patches of approximately equal solid angle, organized in 7 altitude rings (30, 30, 24, 24, 18, 12 and 6 patches) plus a zenith cap.

Returns a float32 tensor of shape [P, 3] (P = 145) on device, one unit vector (x, y, z) per patch centre, with z pointing up (z = cos of the zenith angle). Uses Ladybug's ViewSphere; the result is cached per device for the session.

docs.title: tregenza_solid_angles()
docs.text:
Solid angle of each of the 145 Tregenza patches in steradians (float64).

Built from Ladybug's per-band constants rather than its ViewSphere.tregenza_solid_angles property, which (ladybug-core 0.44) caches its result in the Reinhart attribute and so returns the Reinhart list once reinhart_solid_angles has been read.

docs.title: fetch_tregenza_patch_solid_angles(device)
docs.text: Return a float32 tensor of shape [P] (P = 145) with the solid angle of each Tregenza sky patch in steradians, in the same order as :func:fetch_tregenza_patch_directions (see :func:tregenza_solid_angles). The result is cached per device for the session.

docs.title: compute_radiative_cooling_weights(dewpoint_celsius, bliss_k, device, min_elevation_deg=0.0)
docs.text:
Return a long-wave "cooling potential" weight for each Tregenza sky patch, given an outdoor dew-point temperature.

Scientific background

• Sky (hemispherical) emissivity, εₛky The clear-sky emissivity, integrated over the whole long-wave (thermal infrared) spectrum and the whole hemisphere, can be estimated from near-surface water-vapour content. Martin & Berdahl (1984) fit a quadratic in x = T_dp / 100, with the dew point T_dp in °C, to radiometer measurements of clear skies:

  εₛky(x) = 0.758 + 0.521 x + 0.625 x²                (Eq. 1)

A larger εₛky means the sky behaves more like a blackbody, sending more long-wave radiation back to the surface and therefore offering less cooling potential.

• Directional emissivity (ε_dir) Sky emissivity also depends on the zenith angle θ. Looking up, the line of sight crosses the thinnest layer of atmosphere, so the zenith has the lowest emissivity. Towards the horizon the path through the humid lower air grows like 1/cos θ and the emissivity approaches 1 (a blackbody). Bliss (1961) relates the hemispherical value of Eq. 1 to a direction-dependent value:

  ε_dir(θ) = 1 - (1 - εₛky)^(1 /(k · cos θ))          (Eq. 2)

with k ≈ 1.8 for clear night skies. The code clamps cos θ to at least 1e-3 to avoid division by zero at the horizon (the lowest Tregenza patch centre is at 6° elevation, so the clamp does not change the result in practice).

• Radiative cooling potential Take a horizontal surface that is nearly black in the long wave and at about the air temperature. Its net long-wave loss towards patch p is proportional to the view factor of the patch times the emissivity deficit of that patch:

  w_p ∝ (cos θ_p / π) · Ω_p · (1 - ε_dir(θ_p))      (Eq. 3)

(cos θ_p / π) · Ω_p is the view factor from the horizontal surface to a small patch of solid angle Ω_p. (1 - ε_dir) is the part of the surface's own emission that the sky does not return.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dewpoint_celsius float

Outdoor dew-point temperature [°C]. Acts as a proxy for absolute humidity in Eq. 1. A warning is issued outside [-15, 25] °C, the range treated as valid for the fit.

required bliss_k float

Empirical constant k from Bliss (1961) in Eq. 2. Must be positive; 1.8 is typical for clear skies, and values usually lie between 1.5 and 2.0. A larger k lowers the emissivity near the zenith, which increases the zenith-to-horizon contrast.

required device device

Target compute device for the returned tensor.

required min_elevation_deg float

Design-constraint protection cone: sky patches whose centre elevation is below this angle are excluded (weight 0) and the remaining weights renormalized. This is not part of the physical model. It declares which portion of the sky dome the design protects, similar to obstruction-angle rules in daylight codes. 0 (default) keeps the full hemisphere (pure physical model).

0.0

Returns:

Type Description torch.Tensor (shape [P], P = 145 sky patches, dtype float32)

Cooling weights wᵢ ≥ 0 with Σ wᵢ = 1.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If bliss_k is not positive, or if min_elevation_deg excludes every sky patch.

Notes
  • Assumes a horizontal analysis surface (flat roof). The view factor cos(θ)/π in Eq. 3 is only correct for an upward-facing horizontal surface. For tilted or vertical surfaces the cosine is taken to the surface normal instead, so applying these weights to them over-weights the zenith and under-weights low-altitude patches.
  • Valid for clear nights; clouds would raise εₛky toward unity and flatten the weight distribution.
  • The weights are normalized, dimensionless fractions; they can multiply any radiative heat-transfer quantity in further calculations.
References
  • Bliss, R.W. 1961. "Atmospheric Radiation near the Surface of the Ground." Solar Energy 5 (3): 103-120.
  • Martin, M. & Berdahl, P. 1984. "Characteristics of Infrared Sky Radiation in the United States." Solar Energy 33 (3-4): 321-336.

docs.title: compute_EPW_based_weights(mode, epw_path, hoys, device=None, balance_temperature=15.0, balance_offset=2.0, north=0.0, include_harm=False, simulated_weights=None)
docs.text:
Return a vector of sky-patch weights (length P = 145) derived from EnergyPlus Weather (EPW) data, or from the CIE overcast sky (daylight) or a uniform sky (time-based). Each weight expresses the relative importance of the corresponding Tregenza sky patch for a chosen metric:

┌──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ mode         │ physical meaning of the weight wᵢ            │
├──────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ time-based   │ uniform weight 1 for every patch             │
│ daylight     │ CIE overcast luminance Ω·(1+2 cos θ)/3       │
│ irradiance   │ cumulative solar energy (direct+diffuse)     │
│ benefit      │ net *heating benefit* of solar gains         │
└──────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Scientific background

  • Sky patch geometry: Tregenza subdivides the hemisphere into 145 patches of nearly equal solid angle. fetch_tregenza_patch_directions returns the unit vectors d̂ᵢ = (xᵢ, yᵢ, zᵢ) with zᵢ = cos θᵢ (θ = zenith angle); fetch_tregenza_patch_solid_angles returns the solid angles Ωᵢ.

  • time-based: uninformative baseline, wᵢ = 1 for every patch. Used for carving with traditional time-based solar envelope methods, where every unobstructed sun or sky direction counts equally.

  • daylight: the CIE Standard Overcast Sky (see Darula & Kittler 2002) prescribes a relative luminance L(θ) ∝ (1 + 2 cos θ)/3, three times brighter at the zenith than at the horizon. The weight is that luminance times the patch solid angle Ωᵢ, divided by its sum over the 145 patches: each weight is the patch's share of the overcast sky, and the weights sum to 1 (as the radiative_cooling ones do). A sample point whose whole sky is hidden then counts its whole area, so a daylight score is in m² of fully hidden sky.

  • irradiance: 'SkyMatrix.from_epw' (Ladybug Tools) builds a Perez all-weather sky for every hour, then sums the selected hours ('hoys') to obtain the cumulative short-wave energy per patch:

    wᵢ = Σₜ (E_dirᵢₜ + E_difᵢₜ) [kWh m⁻²]

where E_dirᵢₜ is the direct-beam contribution and E_difᵢₜ the diffuse sky contribution of patch i in hour t.

  • benefit: heating-benefit filter. Only solar gains in hours cold enough to offset heating demand are credited,

    wᵢ = Σₜ (E_dirᵢₜ + E_difᵢₜ) · H( T_bal - ΔT - Tₐₜ )

with the Heaviside step H (1 for a positive argument, else 0) and Tₐₜ the outdoor dry-bulb temperature. The code selects the cold hours from the EPW dry-bulb series and builds a plain cumulative irradiance SkyMatrix over exactly those hours, so the formula above is what is computed. Warm hours in the analysis period contribute nothing, so a longer period does not dilute the result. With include_harm=True (opt-in, experimental) the weights instead follow Ladybug's composite radiation-benefit concept: hot-hour (Tₐ > T_bal + ΔT) radiation is subtracted per patch and the result clipped at zero,

  wᵢ = max( Σ_cold E − Σ_hot E , 0 )

Results then depend on how much of the warm season the analysis period includes. A patch's weight can drop to zero but not below, because a negative weight (the value of shade) cannot be expressed as a carving force. 'balance_temperature' (T_bal) is the building's free-running balance point; derive project-specific values with the Honeybee/EnergyPlus balance-point workflow. 'balance_offset' (ΔT) is the half-width of the dead band around it (hours inside the band count for neither side). With simulated_weights the Heaviside step is replaced by hourly weights in [0, 1] from an ISO 13790 zone model (see :mod:urbansolarcarver.simulated_weights): each hour's irradiance is scaled by benefit[t] (and, with include_harm, harm[t] is subtracted the same way) before the sky matrix is summed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mode (time - based, daylight, irradiance, benefit)

Weighting strategy (see table above). Case and surrounding whitespace are ignored.

'time-based' epw_path str

Path to an EPW file. Required for irradiance and benefit.

required hoys Sequence[float]

Hour-of-year indices (0 to 8759) to sample. Required and non-empty for irradiance and benefit; ignored otherwise. For benefit, a full-year period is a sensible default: the balance filter selects the beneficial hours by itself.

required device device

Compute device for the returned tensor.

'cuda' if available else 'cpu' balance_temperature float

Free-running balance-point temperature T_bal for the benefit filter.

15 °C balance_offset float

Dead-band half-width ΔT: cold hours are below T_bal - ΔT; with include_harm, hot hours are above T_bal + ΔT.

2 °C north float

North direction in degrees clockwise from +Y (USC convention). Converted to Ladybug's counterclockwise convention internally.

0 include_harm bool

Benefit mode only. Subtract hot-hour radiation per patch and clip at zero (experimental, see above).

False simulated_weights tuple of two arrays

Benefit mode only. (benefit, harm) hourly series of length 8760 with values in [0, 1] (the first two items returned by :func:urbansolarcarver.simulated_weights.read_simulated_weights). When given, they replace the balance-point filter and balance_temperature / balance_offset are not used.

None

Returns:

Type Description Tensor

Shape (P,), dtype float32, on device. Weights are non-negative. irradiance and benefit keep the physical scale returned by Ladybug (kWh/m²); daylight weights are shares of the overcast sky and sum to 1, as the weights of :func:compute_radiative_cooling_weights do. The threshold methods (carve_fraction, headtail) are scale-invariant, so the scale does not affect their carving results; a numeric cutoff depends on it. In benefit mode an all-zero vector is returned, with a warning, when no hour in the period qualifies.

Raises:

Type Description TypeError

If mode is not a non-empty string.

FileNotFoundError

If irradiance or benefit is requested without an existing EPW file.

ValueError

If hoys is empty or outside 0 to 8759 for those modes, or if mode is not supported.

RuntimeError

If Ladybug's SkyMatrix does not return P patches.

Notes
  • The EPW-driven modes assume typical meteorology; rare events (e.g. > 99th percentile irradiance) may be under-represented.
  • Without simulated_weights, the benefit filter is purely temperature-based; construction, occupancy and HVAC control logic are not considered.
References
  • Perez, R. et al. 1990. "Modeling daylight availability and irradiance components from direct and global irradiance." Solar Energy 44(5): 271-289.
  • Darula, S. & Kittler, R. 2002. "CIE general sky standard defining luminance distributions." Proceedings eSim 11: 13.
  • Ladybug Tools. "SkyMatrix": cumulative Radiance sky matrix (gendaymtx / Perez all-weather). https://www.ladybug.tools/ladybug-radiance/docs/

docs.title: Sun Vectors
docs.text:
Computes solar position vectors for specified dates and times using Ladybug's sunpath model. Used by the time-based carving mode.

  • get_sun_vectors: returns unit direction vectors pointing toward the sun for each sampled date-time of the analysis period (sun_steps_per_hour per hour), dropping positions below min_altitude and rotating by north_deg. The date-times are local standard time, daylight saving time (time_basis="daylight_saving", one hour ahead on every date) or true solar time (time_basis="solar").
  • sample_period: builds the list of Ladybug date-times of the analysis period that the sun positions are computed for.

docs.title: urbansolarcarver.sun
docs.text:
Sun direction vectors for UrbanSolarCarver.

get_sun_vectors(epw_file, date_list, min_altitude, device, north_deg, time_basis) reads the site location from an EnergyPlus weather (EPW) file, computes the sun position for each Ladybug DateTime (local standard time; daylight saving time, one hour ahead, with time_basis="daylight_saving"; or true solar time with time_basis="solar") with a Ladybug Sunpath, drops positions at or below min_altitude degrees, and returns an (N, 3) float32 tensor of unit vectors pointing from the model toward the sun, in model coordinates.

EPW files are read through the cached weather_file.read_weather_file and Sunpath objects (_initialize_sunpath) are cached, so repeated calls, for example in the daemon, do not re-read or rebuild them.

sample_period turns the analysis period of the preprocessing settings into the Ladybug DateTime list the sun positions are computed for.

docs.title: get_sun_vectors(epw_file, date_list, min_altitude=5.0, device=torch.device('cpu'), north_deg=0.0, time_basis='standard')
docs.text:
Unit vectors toward the sun at the given times, for times when the sun is above min_altitude.

Args: epw_file : Path to the EPW weather file; only its location (latitude, longitude, time zone) is used. date_list : Iterable of Ladybug DateTime objects, in the clock time_basis names. min_altitude: Sun altitude in degrees; times with the sun at or below it are dropped. device : Torch device for the result. north_deg : Model north in degrees clockwise from the +Y axis (USC convention, same as the north_deg setting). Sun vectors are returned in model coordinates. time_basis : "standard": the times are the EPW's local standard time. "daylight_saving": they are daylight saving time, standard time plus one hour, on every date. "solar": they are true solar time, in which the sun crosses the meridian at 12:00.

Returns: A float32 torch.Tensor of shape (N, 3), N <= len(date_list), one unit vector per kept time pointing from the model toward the sun. Empty (0, 3) with a UserWarning if no time is kept.

Raises: ValueError: If date_list is not iterable, is empty or holds non-DateTime items, min_altitude is not a finite number, or time_basis is not one of TIME_BASES. FileNotFoundError, IOError: If the EPW file is missing or unreadable. RuntimeError: If the sun position calculation fails.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
USC uses YAML configuration files. Mode-specific templates are in configs/. Relative paths inside a config file (meshes, EPW, out_dir, simulated_weights_path) are resolved against the folder that contains the YAML file.

From Python, load_config(path, overrides) reads a file and build_config(values) validates values you already hold; both raise ConfigError, which lists the field and message of every problem. A client with no YAML file (the Grasshopper components, through the daemon) starts from the starting values of the chosen mode and applies its overrides. The starting values are the analysis period for time-based (21 Dec, 10:00 to 14:00), irradiance (the full year) and benefit (15 Oct 07:00 to 15 Apr 19:00), tilted_plane_angle_deg: 45 for tilted_plane and carve_fraction: 0.35 for radiative_cooling; the templates in configs/ repeat them. They do not change the schema defaults.

docs.title: Thresholding strategies
docs.text:
After preprocessing computes per-voxel obstruction scores, thresholding decides which voxels to remove. This is the main design control: it sets the trade-off between solar protection and buildable volume.

Mode-specific threshold semantics

The strategies below apply to the weighted modes (irradiance, benefit, daylight, radiative_cooling) whose scores are continuous values.

tilted_plane is strictly binary: a voxel either protrudes above the cut plane (removed) or it does not (kept). Do not set threshold; leave it unset (None). Setting a string method or a value > 0 raises a validation error.

time-based scores are shaded area x duration in m²·h (how much protected surface the voxel shades, and for how long, during the period). Use a non-negative number: threshold: 0 removes any voxel that shadows at any sampled moment (strict, default); threshold: 5 tolerates up to 5 m²·h; and so on. See Modes: violation-count thresholds for details.

carve_fraction (recommended for weighted modes) : Removes a fraction of the total obstruction weight of the building's voxels, counting what carve_above removes. Set carve_fraction: 0.7 to remove 70% of the obstruction (aggressive: taller, slimmer result with better solar access). Set carve_fraction: 0.3 for a conservative result (bulkier volume, more floor area). It works as a solar protection slider.

headtail : Jiang (2013) head/tail breaks: splits the scores at their mean and keeps splitting the upper part while it holds at most 40% of the values. Designed for heavy-tailed score distributions where most voxels have low scores and a few have very high scores. Biased toward removing only the worst obstructors.

Numeric value (e.g., threshold: 0.35) : Manual cutoff on the scores, in the mode's score unit: kWh for irradiance and benefit, m² of fully hidden sky for daylight and radiative_cooling, m²·h for time-based (see Modes). Carves all voxels scoring above this value. Set diagnostic_plots: true to get the score histogram and pick a value from it.

Tip

The decomposed pipeline is designed for threshold exploration. Compute scores once (preprocessing), then re-run thresholding with different parameters; it takes seconds because the ray tracing is already done.

docs.title: CLI overrides
docs.text:
Any config value can be overridden from the command line:

urbansolarcarver preprocessing -c config.yaml     -o voxel_size=0.5     -o mode=irradiance     -o threshold=carve_fraction

Relative paths given in overrides are resolved against the current directory, not the YAML's folder.

docs.title: Output structure
docs.text:
With the default output folders (<out_dir>/preprocessing, <out_dir>/thresholding, <out_dir>/exporting, and <out_dir>/massing when massing runs):

outputs/
  preprocessing/
    scores.npy, voxel_grid.npy, footprint.json, test_points.npy, test_normals.npy, manifest.json, diagnostics/
  thresholding/
    mask.npy, manifest.json, diagnostics/
  exporting/
    export.ply (or .obj/.stl/.glb), manifest.json, diagnostics/
  massing/
    plates.json, plates.obj (and plates.ply/.stl/.glb), manifest.json, diagnostics/
  run_report.md

Every manifest carries a run_id, new on each run of its stage, and the manifests after preprocessing record the run_id they were built from. A stage refuses an upstream that was re-run since (StageChainError, naming the stage to re-run), so re-run preprocessing once for a run folder written by an earlier version.

Weighted modes also write preprocessing/patch_weights.npy.

docs.title: Quick setup (recommended)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/avarth/UrbanSolarCarver.git
cd UrbanSolarCarver
python setup_env.py

This creates a virtual environment (.venv/ in the repository; on Windows it falls back to ~/.usc-venv when the repository path is too long for the 260-character path limit), reads the CUDA version from your NVIDIA driver, asks the PyTorch wheel indexes that driver can run which torch they offer and installs the newest, installs USC in editable mode together with the browser UI (the ui extra), and precompiles the Warp kernels.

python setup_env.py --cpu             # force CPU-only (no CUDA)
python setup_env.py --dry-run         # show what would be installed
python setup_env.py --no-ui           # leave out the browser UI (the ui extra)
python setup_env.py --venv-dir PATH   # put the virtual environment at PATH

docs.title: Manual installation
docs.text:
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/activate          # Windows
# source .venv/bin/activate     # Linux/macOS

pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126
pip install -e .[dev,ui]       # leave out ,ui if you do not want the browser UI

Pick the PyTorch index for your driver on https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/ (nvidia-smi shows the highest CUDA version the driver supports; python setup_env.py --dry-run shows the index the installer would choose). PyTorch stops publishing to older indexes, so prefer one that still receives releases.

An editable install keeps the version number it was installed with. After pulling a new version, refresh it with pip install -e . --no-deps so usc --version reports it.

docs.title: Browser UI
docs.text:
The browser interface is an optional extra of the package (ui). setup_env.py installs it unless --no-ui is given. To add it to an existing environment:

python -m pip install -e ".[ui]"

Then start it by double-clicking start-urbansolarcarver.bat (Windows) or running ./start-urbansolarcarver.sh (Linux, macOS) in the repository folder; on a fresh clone the launcher runs setup_env.py first. From a terminal, usc ui does the same. Without the extra, every other usc command works as before, and usc ui prints the install command above and exits.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
Run the full pipeline in one call:

from urbansolarcarver import load_config, run_pipeline

cfg = load_config("config.yaml")
result = run_pipeline(cfg, out_dir="./outputs")
print(f"Carved mesh: {result.exporting.export_path}")

Or run stages individually for finer control:

from urbansolarcarver import load_config, preprocessing, thresholding, exporting
from pathlib import Path

cfg = load_config("config.yaml")

# Stage 1: compute per-voxel carving scores
pre = preprocessing(cfg, Path("outputs/preprocessing"))

# Stage 2: apply threshold to create binary mask
thr = thresholding(pre, cfg, Path("outputs/thresholding"))

# Stage 3: reconstruct mesh from mask
exp = exporting(thr, cfg, Path("outputs/exporting"))

The decomposed workflow lets you re-run thresholding with different parameters without recomputing scores.

Relative paths inside config.yaml are resolved against the YAML file's folder; the out_dir arguments above are relative to the current directory.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
# Run stages sequentially
urbansolarcarver preprocessing -c config.yaml
urbansolarcarver thresholding -c config.yaml -f outputs/preprocessing/manifest.json
urbansolarcarver exporting -c config.yaml -f outputs/thresholding/manifest.json

# Override config values on the fly
urbansolarcarver preprocessing -c config.yaml -o voxel_size=0.5 -o mode=irradiance

# View all config options
urbansolarcarver schema

docs.title: Input Requirements
docs.text:
• Max volume mesh: watertight mesh (PLY recommended; any format Trimesh reads) representing the theoretical maximum buildable volume.
  • Test surface mesh: planar faces whose solar/daylight access is to be protected. Each face must be a flat panel.
  • EPW weather file: hourly climate data for the site location (required for time-based, irradiance and benefit; not used by daylight, tilted_plane or radiative_cooling).
  • All meshes must share the same coordinate system and units (meters recommended).
